notes: ACCESS: the storefront is a client-side React SPA (empty shell to plain curl and to WebFetch), but the Magento 2 backend behind it exposes an UNAUTHENTICATED GraphQL endpoint at https://www.swooneditions.com/graphql (POST, curl_cffi impersonate=chrome; no proxy, no impersonation sweep, no interstitial work needed), which is the site's own data layer. Route confirmed by notes/49.md from the prior Home-Decor pass. TREE: pulled all 1115 category nodes with categories(pageSize:300,currentPage:N,filters:{}) paged 4x, cross-checked against the rendered mega-menu obtained through r.jina.ai (which renders the SPA nav). The mega-menu's own 'BY TYPE' lists under Storage, Tables, Chairs, Sofas, Footstools and Beds are exactly the leaf set emitted here. COUNTS: this storefront publishes NO rendered 'N products' header anywhere - not in the mega-menu, not on category landing pages, not on the listing grids (checked storage/sideboards and chairs/armchairs rendered through r.jina.ai). Method 1 is therefore unobtainable, so I used methods 2+3 together: products(filter:{category_id:{eq:ID}}).total_count, AND for every one of the 37 leaves I enumerated the category to exhaustion at pageSize 100 following page_info.total_pages and counted unique SKUs. In all 37 the unique-SKU count equalled total_count exactly and also equalled the categories.product_count field, so the Magento product_count that the brief flags as inflated elsewhere survives an exhaustion check on this store. Every leaf was then re-read about 40 minutes later: zero drift on all 37. URL VALIDATION: every emitted URL was resolved through route(url:...) and returns the CategoryTree expected; a control path ('zzz-not-a-real-page') returns null, so the resolver genuinely discriminates rather than always answering. That resolver also exposed stale alias nodes whose stored url_path is not their canonical one - /tables/desks and /study/desks both resolve to cat 675 ('desks'), /sleeping/sofa-beds resolves to cat 668 ('sofas/sofa-beds'), /dining-room/dining-chairs resolves to cat 21 ('chairs/dining-chairs'), /dining-room/dining-tables to cat 159 and /bedroom/beds to cat 666. Those aliases are collapsed rather than emitted twice. ROOM TREE EXCLUDED, WITH PROOF: Swoon has a 'Shop by > BY ROOM' nav (Living room, Bedroom, Dining room, Hallway, Home office, Kitchen, Bathroom, Outdoor). I enumerated every furniture child of it and compared SKU sets against the union of the 37 emitted type leaves (1361 unique SKUs). They are pure room facets - products unique to each, out of its own total: Living Room Chairs 0/99, LR Sofas 0/219, LR Storage 1/357, LR Tables 1/214, Dining Room Storage 0/184, Hallway Storage 1/189, Hallway Tables 0/35, Hallway Chairs 0/24, Bedroom Storage 1/170, Bedroom Tables 0/200, Bedroom Chairs 0/48, Home Office Chairs 0/7, Home Office Storage 0/166, Kitchen 0/118. Each contributes 0 or 1 products not already covered, so emitting them would double-count the same catalogue. /bathrooms resolves to a CMS page, not a category - there is no bathroom furniture. Kitchen (cat 201, 118) is genuinely kitchen furniture by content (url_key scan: 33 shelving, 27 cabinets, 13 stools, 11 trolleys, 9 tables, 1 bench, plus 17 lighting and 2 mirrors mis-tagged in) but is 100% contained in the type leaves, so it is a room re-cut too. OTHER FACETS DROPPED, EACH PROVEN BY SKU-SET COMPARISON RATHER THAN BY NAME: Bespoke sofas (210) is 210/210 inside the seat-count+corner+sofa-bed union; Bespoke chairs (61) is 61/61 inside Armchairs+Occasional chairs+Love seats; Bespoke Footstools (33) sits entirely inside Footstools/Ottomans; the whole 'Bespoke furniture' department (cat 163, 306) duplicates those same nodes. Velvet Sofas (208) is 208/208 inside the sofa union (material facet). Chesterfield sofas (10) is a style cut absent from the mega-menu. 'Patterned Furniture' (16) is a marketing collection and 15 of its 16 are already covered. All level-4 nodes under coffee/side/console/bedside/dining tables, bed frames, corner sofas, TV stands, sideboards, cabinets, chests of drawers, wardrobes, shelving and desks are colour/material/shape/size filter re-cuts (Black/White/Grey/Wooden/Marble/Glass/Round/Small/Large/Tall/Slim/King size/Double/Super king/Upholstered/Metal/Left-Hand/Right-Hand) and are dropped per the filter-page rule, with their parents kept as the leaves. Delivery/availability facets (Speedy sofas/chairs/tables/storage/desks/footstools, In Stock *, Clearance beds) and marketing nodes (New In, Bestsellers, Flash SALE, Clearance, Delivery by Christmas, Almost/Not Perfect, Collections, Editions, the 628-node Range and Swoon Selects range pages, The Essentials, EmilySixty Edit, Made in Britain, Get Some Space, Influencer gifting, the style branches Art deco/Mid-century/Industrial/Classic/Contemporary/Scandi, Gift cards, Swatches and 'Test & Utility cat') are excluded per section 3. NON-FURNITURE EXCLUDED: Lighting and all its children and room cuts, Mirrors, Rugs, Curtains, Bedding and the Accessories nodes - those belong to the Lighting / Wall Decor / textile tasks. Storage boxes (cat 174, /storage/storage-boxes, 3 SKUs: 2 storage boxes + 1 ottoman) excluded as standalone storage goods per the storage-vs-furniture line. Swoon sells no mattresses. COMPLETENESS: I keyword-swept all 1115 category nodes for furniture slugs (sofa|chair|table|desk|bed|stool|bench|cabinet|sideboard|chest|wardrobe|shelv|shelf|bookcase|console|dresser|tv-stand|media|footstool|ottoman|pouffe|seat|storage|furnitur|trolley|armoire|nightstand|vanity|cot|crib|nursery|rack) after stripping the known marketing/filter/delivery branches; the survivors are exactly the nodes accounted for above, so nothing furniture-shaped in the catalogue is unhandled. Swoon has no kids/nursery furniture and no bathroom furniture.
